title: Ops QuickSplice: seller pocket (draft)
body:
Purpose: ultra-compact, ops-forward seller pocket for pilot/onramp conversations. Goal is to get an engineer nod + legal triage within first pilot call. This is intentionally terse — meant for SEs doing 2-4 pilot calls per day.

Topline 15s opener:
- "We’re Redwood Inference — predictable, low-latency model serving across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. For pilots we prioritize a single measurable outcome: get 1x integrated route with our SDK and a smoke-test dataset in 14 days."

Target persona(s):
- Platform/Integration Architect (latency and routing constraints)
- ML infra/ML engineer (model footprint, quantization, KV caching)
- Product PM (success metric: accuracy + cost per inference)

60s value thread (short):
- Reduce token unit cost by 20–40% for typical seq lengths via batching + KV caching
- SLA-backed dedicated capacity for predictable throughput when needed
- Simple rollback and canary wiring in the Console so product teams can A/B model variants without infra work

Rapid qualification questions (use as checklist):
- What is your 95p latency target for 512-token requests?
- Peak qps and typical sequence length distribution?
- Are you comfortable sharing a 1k sample prompt set for quality baseline?
- Any data residency / VPC/KMS constraints?

Three fast-play scenarios + scripts:
1) Latency-first pilot (mobile assistant)
- Ask: "What's your 95p currently and tolerable degradation during burst?"
- Play: propose hosted API PoC with dedicated pool reserved for pilot hours; instrument latency dashboards; enable prefix caching for welcome flows.
- Fallback: if hosted latency not meeting 95p, route critical traffic to a smaller quantized variant pinned to Dedicated.

2) Cost-constrained POC (high-volume embeddings)
- Ask: "Embeddings per month? reuse patterns?"
- Play: suggest hybrid: local cache + batched embedding job + private early-stage dedicated pool. Recommend 8-bit quantization profile and async batching to maximize throughput.
- Fallback: time-boxed run of caching + batch tuning; if quality regresses, short A/B versus full-precision model.

3) Regulated / VPC pilot (legal heavy)
- Ask: "Do you need on-prem or VPC with HSM/KMS?"
- Play: push Redwood Private quickstart (control plane & audit) + isolated dedicated worker lanes; pre-approve SOC/Security docs and KMS flow.
- Fallback: narrow scope to non-prod dataset in our hosted region with strict retention + legal NDA while Private onboarding proceeds.

Fallback matrix (one-liners SE cuebook):
- Model quality drop -> revert to prior model version + notify PM + run small eval set
- Latency spike -> shift traffic to lower-latency variant or increase pool size for pilot hours
- Cost runaway -> enable hard budget throttle + increase cache window for repeating prompts
- Compliance hold -> pause production routing; switch to redacted/sampled logging and handoff to security lead

Pilot deliverables & 14-day checklist (minimum viable pilot):
- Day 0: sign MOU, provisional SOW for pilot hours, Slack + shared drive access
- Day 1-3: SDK integration + smoke test, initial telemetry capture (latency, errors, tokens)
- Day 4-8: tune batching/caching, run quality baseline eval on 1k prompts, document divergences
- Day 9-12: stress and run gating scenarios (burst, cold-start), finalize fallback plan
- Day 13-14: demo + go/no-go decision; capture cost per 1k tokens and 95p latency with chosen model variant

Metrics to capture (add to pilot dashboard):
- 95p latency, median latency, p99 under burst
- tokens/second per GPU, cost per 1k tokens, cache hit rate
- model regression % vs baseline eval (precision/recall or task-specific metric)
- end-to-end success rate for production-like calls

Objection handling snippets (short):
- "We built it in-house": "Totally — teams that switch to Redwood usually keep experimentation internally but offload serving. We focus on predictable economics and operational playbooks so your engineers can work on product, not infra."
- "Vendor lock-in" : "You control model versions, region placement, and there’s a private deployment option; rollback and canary controls are API-first so migration is reversible."
- "Cost concerns": "We start pilot with a cost baseline and a hard throttle; Optimize recommendations (batch sizes/quant profiles) are included to improve unit economics quickly."

Demo checklist (what SE should show in 8 minutes):
- Console: route config, real-time latency graph, active model variant toggle
- SDK: 3-line call, streaming response, error handling snippet
- Rollout: canary toggle + automatic fallback policy example

Open questions / risky assumptions (notes to self):
- Legal turnaround time for some customers is typically 3–6 weeks; pilot timeline must account for that
- Expect variance in token-length distributions; ensure demo prompts represent customer data
- Need quickmapping of engineering owners who can approve VPN/KMS (ask CS for contacts before call)

Immediate TODOs (owner tags):
- Avery: create a 2-slide demo pack with 3 sample prompts (due EOD)
- Maya: update the quickstart SDK snippet for the latest auth flow (PR link in linked_artifacts)
- Liam: assemble SOC/HSM one-pager for Private quickstarts

Notes-to-self / copyable snippets: 
- "14-day integration promise: smoke test + baseline eval + cost report."
- Slack cue: "@ops-alerts start pilot: <cust-name> — reserved pool: 8 GPUs, pilot hours: 9a-5p PT M-F"

Versioning / lifecycle: this is a living seller pocket — iterate after first 5 pilots. Keep this doc extremely short, port canonical demo slides into Confluence / demo repo after first customer.

Raw playbook reference links (for SE kit):
- Confluence quickstart: confluence:GTM/ops-quicksplice-landing
- Pilot JIRA: JIRA:GTM-1107
- SDK snippet PR: github:docs/quicksplice-cards#12

End.
